findings.title: Team admin/owner permission check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, which is only true for a user who is both admin and owner. Despite the name, a team admin (or the owner, depending on how the helpers classify roles) will be denied. The check should be `||`. Consequence: legitimate team admins/owners who are neither the booking organizer nor an attendee get FORBIDDEN.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw input instead of the filtered new guests
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered request input. In email-manager, membership in this array decides whether an attendee receives the "scheduled" email (treated as a newly added guest) or the "guests added" notice. Emails that were filtered out (already-existing attendees, blacklisted addresses) are still in `guests`, so pre-existing attendees will receive a full booking-confirmation email as if they were just invited. `uniqueGuests` should be passed instead.

findings.title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive against lowercased list
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased when parsed, but the guest email is compared as-is (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). A blacklisted address submitted with any uppercase character (e.g. `Spam@x.com`) bypasses the filter. Lowercase the guest before comparison. The same case-sensitivity also lets duplicate attendees be created with differing case.

findings.title: Email failure swallowed without logging the error
findings.body: The catch block logs a fixed string via `console.log` and discards `err`, making email delivery failures impossible to diagnose. Use the project logger and include the error and bookingId.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores eventType disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Every other sender in this file accepts `eventTypeMetadata` and skips host/attendee mail when `disableStandardEmails.all.host/attendee` is set. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and unconditionally sends to organizer, team members and all attendees, so event types that have standard emails disabled will still emit mail, violating the configured behaviour.

findings.title: Organizer subject dereferences attendees[0] and uses an empty guest name
findings.body: `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` will throw if the attendee list is empty, and newly added guests are created with `name: ""`, so the subject can render as "Guests Added:  with  at ..." when the first attendee is a name-less guest. Guard the access and fall back to the attendee email.

findings.title: Initial empty email row always fails validation
findings.body: `multiEmailValue` is initialised to `[""]`, and `handleAdd` only early-returns on a zero-length array. If the user clicks Add without typing, the `""` entry fails `z.string().email()` and the generic "Emails must be unique and valid" error is shown instead of a prompt to enter an email; similarly an extra blank row added via "Add another" blocks submission with a confusing message. Filter out empty strings before validating.

findings.title: Error toast fallback is dead code and shows raw tRPC code
findings.body: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` is always a non-empty string, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never falls back. Users see strings like "FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission" (and `undefined: ...` when `err.data` is missing) rather than a localized message.

findings.title: MultiEmail imports from the @calcom/ui barrel that re-exports it, creating a cycle
findings.body: `packages/ui/index.tsx` now exports `MultiEmail` from `./form/MultiEmailLazy`, while `MultiEmail.tsx` imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui` — the same barrel. This circular dependency can cause undefined components at module-init time in some bundling/SSR orders. Import directly from the component paths like other files in `packages/ui/form` do.

findings.title: No tests for the new addGuests handler
findings.body: The handler contains non-trivial authorization, dedup/blacklist filtering and calendar/email side effects, but no unit tests were added. At minimum the permission branches (organizer / attendee / team role) and the duplicate-and-blacklist filtering should be covered to prevent regressions in an endpoint that writes attendees and sends mail.
